assessment: The measured holes are shut: Whiptongue closed sweepers, Deathgorge closed graveyard, Yeva removed the one-spell flash cap, and the goldfish now means 3.767 bodies by turn 6. What is left to buy is not consistency — it is unmodeled power and the field's table data, so the ten ranks the untap/flash engine class and the consensus payoffs the recon says 45-61% of Radagast lists run and this 99 still lacks. The back of the list stays doors: Seedborn Muse is the confirmed Game Changer whose pairing with the now-sleeved Yeva makes the whole hand castable on everyone's turn, and Springheart/Nissa carry the recorded bracket-4 infinite. No entry is premised on flashing a finisher — stack 005 settled that the kill is a main-phase act.

ten.why: With Yeva in the 99 every green creature in hand has flash but the mana still refills once a round; Muse untaps it in every other untap step, so the pair converts a full grip into a cast on all four turns — the exact engine class the recon says the field runs and this 99 lacks, and nothing the goldfish can model.
ten.unlocks: The power door: floor moves 1 to 3, landing exactly on the target — a confirmed Game Changer, so it is a pod conversation before it is a purchase.

ten.why: Selvala is still the declared one-card class, drawn 12.3% by turn 6, and the diagnosis names Henge the only backup: a draw per nontoken body plus {G}{G} a turn, discounted toward five mana by any power-4 board. 45% of recorded lists run it; its cost reduction is exactly the kind of power the simulation cannot price.
ten.unlocks: The gas engine stops resting on one legend, and the {G}{G} funds the ambush on turns the lands are already spent.

ten.why: The field's top absent add at 61% of ~800 lists: an artifact or enchantment dies (or a land lands, or 4 life) on every creature cast, which in a deck casting creatures on all four turns is the repeatable, non-combat-facing interaction the diagnosis says the trap suite lacks.
ten.unlocks: Interaction that scales with the metronome itself — Ravenous Sailback's one-shot mode, every single turn.

ten.why: 59% of recorded lists run it and the diagnosis's card-advantage reading explains why: only Beast Whisperer draws ungated here — Soul draws on every nontoken body with no power gate, no combat, no deaths, on a 6/6 trample frame that anchors Stampede and Ibex's greatest-power X.
ten.unlocks: A second ungated per-body engine, so a board of small bodies still pays a card each.

ten.why: The aggregate's top flash trap at 48%: flashed for {2}{G}{G}{G} it fights a creature on arrival, smashes an artifact or enchantment on every attack — and the Human clause is live here, bouncing Eternal Witness to rebuy her recursion while Kogla goes indestructible, with Radagast discounting the recast.
ten.unlocks: An ambush that is removal, a 7/6 attacker, and a Witness engine in one slot — three unmodeled jobs the sim prices at zero.

ten.why: Still the thinnest engine component — finisher plus second wave 40.2% by turn 6, bodies at 3.767 against stack 003's five-body bar; Avenger makes six-plus Plants at once on this 36-land base, and stack 006 verified end-step tokens attack at dawn.
ten.unlocks: The widest one-card second wave in the colour: one Avenger end step makes the next main-phase Stampede lethal.

ten.card: Disciple of Freyalise // Garden of Freyalise
ten.why: 48% of recorded lists: a land drop in the opening hand, and late a flashed body that converts a doomed creature into its power in cards — the wrath-response the deck can cast in the sweeper's window, holding up exactly the mana it already banks.
ten.unlocks: A card that is never dead: mana when behind, a Craterhoof's worth of cards when the board is about to be taken anyway.

ten.why: The article's named flash trap: dropped before blocks, all combat damage to your other creatures becomes +1/+1 counters, turning any red sweeper or alpha strike into a bigger board — priced honestly, it also switches Hornet Nest OFF, since prevented damage makes no Insects.
ten.unlocks: Combat maths no opponent can read while four mana is open; the shuffle-home clause means it never stays dead.

combo_lines_opened.produces: Infinite landfall triggers; infinite tapped land tokens

ten.why: Held out of the 99 by the bracket-3 target: the combo index records a two-card infinite with Tireless Provisioner, who is in the deck, so sleeving it moves the computed floor from 1 to 4 — and it sits in the build's own pool file.
ten.unlocks: The bracket-4 door: bestowed on any body it makes a copy or an Insect on every land drop at bracket-3 tempo, with the recorded infinite behind it. The line needs a stack scenario before it is claimed as a kill.

combo_lines_opened.produces: Infinite landfall triggers; infinite tapped land tokens

ten.why: The other half of the benched pair, also in the pool file: alone it fires no bracket signal and answers no measured deficit — its recorded infinite needs Springheart, so it matters only if both come in together.
ten.unlocks: Mana on every land drop, an Elf or Elemental to hand on the second — and the second key to the bracket-4 door. Unverified until a stack scenario runs the loop.

gaps: Temur Sabertooth is the highest-unmodeled-power card that missed the ten: the recon's bounce-to-recast engine (rebuy any ETB at Radagast's discount, protect any body) rests on one source — a stub list — and this ranking privileged the widely-agreed claims; table data would promote it.

Ezuri's Predation's open question is now moot in one direction — Whiptongue closed the sweeper axis — but whether a 35-creature deck wants a symmetric wipe AT ALL is still the research-strategy question; nothing here re-litigates it.

Mosswort Bridge (43%) was not ranked: the manabase's hypergeometric already declined a colourless utility land (Emergence Zone) in favour of a Forest, and no new evidence overturns that adjudication — hideaway's fit is real, but the scorer owns the land slots.

The Springheart + Tireless Provisioner line is the combo index's record and the index is format-agnostic; a /resolve-stack run settles whether the loop's mana closes in this 99 before the bracket-4 door opens.
Whether Selvala's tapped mana pays for a flashed cast in her own window remains the open diagnosis question; its answer prices The Great Henge as backup versus upgrade and could move it to first.
Recon percentages describe first movers (~800 mostly-precon lists, 64 upgraded); the 45-61% figures are leads, not verdicts.
